text:
Kasperi Kapanen is on his fourth NHL team, and in Edmonton he has found real minutes: 18:05 a night, more than many of the Oilers' forwards. He's turned them into 13 points in 23 games, seven of them on the power play, plus seven points in his last ten.

The question is whether the role fits the player. Evolving-Hockey's read of his 2025-26 wasn't kind on offense (his team created less with him on the ice, bottom 5% of forwards), and this season Edmonton gets 48% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him out there, about even with what it does without him. He's shooting 20% on 30 shots, well above the league's 13.4, with six goals on 4.28 expected. That part will likely cool.

What he brings is speed and clean exits: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 80% of his zone exits leaving with possession last season. He also has 49 hits. On a team built around Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl, a winger who moves the puck up the ice cleanly can earn a spot. The power-play production is the part to watch.
headline: Kapanen is playing up the lineup in Edmonton
